title: 14 — Data Terminology A to Z
html:
14 — Data Terminology A to Z

The one idea: most confusion in a data platform is vocabulary. This is one place with every term used across the open-lakehouse, data-engineering and financial-data sets, each explained in a sentence or two, with a pointer to where it is covered in depth.

1. How to use this

  • Terms are grouped by first letter. Each entry gives a plain definition and, where useful, a link to more.
  • General data-engineering terms (ETL, OLAP, SCD and so on) are also in the Data Engineering glossary. This list focuses on lakehouse, governance, document AI and financial-data terms.
  • Status-sensitive product terms carry the date they were checked (2026-10-26).

2. A to E

Term Meaning
ABAC Attribute-based access control. Access rules driven by tags on data (for example "mask every column tagged PII") instead of per-table rules. GA in Unity Catalog in 2026 (05)
Acquisition manifest The record of what was collected, from where, when, under which rights, with its content hash
ADBC Arrow Database Connectivity: a database API that returns Arrow data (04)
ADLS Gen2 Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2: Blob Storage with a hierarchical namespace, used as lakehouse storage
Agent A program that uses a language model to decide which tools to call to reach a goal
AI Functions Databricks SQL functions that call models: ai_query, ai_extract, ai_classify, ai_parse_document (09)
AMC Asset management company: the firm that runs mutual fund schemes
AMFI Association of Mutual Funds in India. Publishes daily NAVs and scheme codes
Anomaly detection Monitoring that learns a table's normal pattern (freshness, completeness) and flags breaks (13)
Append-only Storage where rows are only added, never changed in place. Corrections are new rows
Arrow Apache Arrow, the shared in-memory columnar format (04)
As-of query A query for the state of data at a past time, on valid time, knowledge time or both
Atomic publish Making a whole batch visible in one step, or none of it
AUM Assets under management: the total value a fund or AMC manages
AUTO CDC Lakeflow's declarative CDC (formerly APPLY CHANGES), producing SCD1 or SCD2 tables (06)
Benchmark mapping Linking each fund to the index it is measured against
Bitemporal Two time axes per row: valid time (true in the world) and knowledge time (when we learned it)
BM25 The standard keyword-ranking formula in full-text search (09)
Bonus issue Free extra shares given to shareholders. The price adjusts, so history must be adjusted to compare
Bounding box Page coordinates [x0, y0, x1, y1] of an extracted value: the evidence a reviewer checks
Branch (Iceberg) A named, movable line of snapshots. Used for write-audit-publish (02)
Bronze, Silver, Gold As received / checked and conformed / certified for consumption. Also called the medallion layers
BRSR Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: SEBI's ESG disclosure for large listed companies
Canary release Sending a small slice of live traffic to a new model or code version before full release
Cap table Who owns what share of a private company
Catalog The service that maps table names to metadata and governs access (Unity Catalog, Polaris and others) (03)
CDC Change data capture: reading inserts, updates and deletes from a database's log instead of re-reading tables
Certification A named person signing a frozen dataset release as fit to publish
Checkpoint Saved progress of a reader (offset, sequence, file list) so a restart resumes correctly
Chunking Splitting documents into passages for search and retrieval
CIN Corporate Identity Number: the 21-character Indian company registration id
Clean room A governed space where parties compute on combined data and only approved results leave (08)
Column mask A function that hides or alters a column's values depending on who is asking
Compaction Rewriting many small files (and their deletes) into fewer, larger files
Confidence score A model's estimate of how likely an extracted value is right. Drives auto-accept or review
Connected components Groups of nodes linked by any path. Used to cluster matched records (12)
Contagion Stress spreading through links: group companies, common lenders, guarantees
Copy-on-write Applying a change by rewriting affected files (02)
Corporate action An event that changes a security: split, bonus, dividend, merger, rights issue
Correction Fixing a value that was wrong when published. A new version with reason and approver
Corroboration How many independent sources agree on a fact
Covenant A condition in a loan agreement, such as a maximum leverage ratio
Credential vending A catalog issuing short-lived storage credentials scoped to one table
Data contract A versioned, testable promise about a dataset's schema, quality, freshness and owner (ODCS)
Data profiling Computing statistics and their drift over time for a table
Deletion vector A bitmap marking deleted rows in a data file (Iceberg v3, Delta)
DPDP Act India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Its Rules were notified in November 2025, with phased duties (17)
Delta Lake Open table format from the Linux Foundation, the default on Databricks
Delta Sharing Open protocol to share live tables without copying them (08)
Derive (right) Licence permission to create new data from a source
Divergence Disagreement between sources. Can be a signal in itself
Drift A change in a data or model distribution over time
ECL Expected credit loss: the forward-looking loan-loss provision under Ind AS 109
Embedding A numeric vector representing meaning, used for similarity search
Entitlement What a caller may access, decided from identity, subscription, source rights, purpose and quota
Entity resolution Deciding which records refer to the same real-world entity
Entity spine The master list of entities with one id each, and every source id mapped to it
Equality delete A delete file listing values; rows matching them are deleted (Iceberg v2)
ESG Environmental, social and governance data
Evidence pointer A link from a fact to its file, page and box, or row
Exception queue A work list of items that need human judgement, with evidence and SLAs
Expectation A declarative row-level quality rule in Lakeflow pipelines, with warn, drop or fail behaviour
External location A Unity Catalog object granting access to a cloud storage path
External table A table whose files UC governs but does not own

3. F to M

Term Meaning
Fair value Price an asset would fetch in an orderly sale. Mark-to-market uses it
Fast-forward Moving one Iceberg branch to the head of another, atomically
FIBO Financial Industry Business Ontology, from the EDM Council. A standard vocabulary of financial concepts
Fine-tuning Further training a pre-trained model on your own labelled examples
Flight SQL SQL over Arrow Flight, a columnar network protocol
Foreign table A table whose metadata another catalog owns. UC governs reads
Four-eyes Two different people must act: one proposes, one approves
Freshness How recently a table received the data it should have
Frontier model The most capable general-purpose model from a major provider, usually called over an API
G-sec Government security: a bond issued by the Government of India
Gate A checkpoint between stages that can say no, and records every decision
Golden copy, golden record The single trusted version of an entity or fact
Golden set Human-labelled examples used to evaluate models before release
Governed tag An admin-controlled tag used for access policy, classification and cost
GST Goods and Services Tax. Return data can signal SME turnover, with consent
Hidden partitioning Iceberg derives partition values from a column, so queries filter the column itself
Hybrid search Combining keyword and vector search, then fusing the rankings
Iceberg Apache Iceberg, an open table format (01)
Idempotent Running it twice gives the same result as running it once
Immutable landing Storing every received file unchanged, hashed and locked
Information barrier Rules that keep certain data apart between teams to avoid conflicts of interest
InvIT, REIT Infrastructure and real estate investment trusts: listed vehicles holding income-producing assets
ISIN International Securities Identification Number: a 12-character security id
KS statistic Kolmogorov-Smirnov: the largest gap between two cumulative distributions, used for drift (16)
Knowledge graph Entities, documents, definitions and relationships linked as a graph, used as context
Knowledge time When the platform learned a fact. Also called transaction time or system time
Lakebase Databricks-managed PostgreSQL next to the lakehouse (10)
Lakeflow Databricks' ingestion (Connect), pipelines (Declarative Pipelines) and orchestration (Jobs)
Lakehouse Federation Querying external databases through Unity Catalog without ingesting them
Layout parsing Detecting a page's blocks, reading order, tables and figures before extracting text
LEI Legal Entity Identifier: a 20-character global id for legal entities (ISO 17442)
Liquid clustering Flexible, incremental data layout on chosen keys, replacing fixed partitions
LLM judge A language model used to score another model's output against criteria
LoggedModel MLflow 3's entity tying a model or app version to code, config, traces and evaluations
Look-through holdings A fund-of-funds' exposure to the securities held by the funds it owns
MAD Median absolute deviation: a spread measure that outliers can't inflate, used in robust z-scores
Maker-checker Same as four-eyes: maker proposes, checker approves
Managed table A table whose storage and lifecycle Unity Catalog owns
Manifest (Iceberg) Avro file listing data files with per-column statistics
Mark-to-market Valuing holdings at current market or fair prices
MCP Model Context Protocol: an open protocol for agents to discover and call tools
Merge-on-read Applying a change by writing delete markers, merged at read time
Metering Recording usage per caller, product and call, for billing and audit
Metric view A Unity Catalog object defining measures and dimensions once, queried with MEASURE()
MLflow Open-source platform for experiment tracking, model registry, tracing and evaluation
Model Serving Databricks service hosting models behind REST endpoints

4. N to S

Term Meaning
NAV Net asset value per unit of a mutual fund scheme, published daily
NPA Non-performing asset: a loan whose interest or principal is overdue beyond the regulator's threshold (generally 90 days in India)
Nowcast An estimate of a current or very recent value before official data is published
OCR Optical character recognition: turning images of text into text
ODCS Open Data Contract Standard, v3.1.0 from Bitol (13)
OLTP, OLAP Many small transactional reads and writes / large analytical scans and aggregates
Ontology A formal model of concepts, their properties and relationships, with identifiers
Open weights A model whose trained weights are published, so you can self-host it
OpenLineage Open event specification for lineage: runs, jobs, inputs, outputs, facets
Orphan file A file in table storage that no snapshot references
PAN Permanent Account Number: the 10-character Indian tax id
Parquet Apache Parquet, the columnar file format (04)
PD Probability of default over a horizon, usually one year
Peer set A group of comparable entities used for benchmarking
Perimeter The boundary inside which documents may be processed
Photon Databricks' vectorised C++ query engine
Pledge (promoter) Shares a promoter has pledged as loan collateral. High pledges are a risk signal
Position delete A delete file naming file and row positions (Iceberg v2)
Predictive optimization Automatic table maintenance on Unity Catalog managed tables
Prompt injection Text that tries to override a model's instructions. Indirect when planted in documents or tool output (18)
PSI Population stability index: drift measure comparing shares per bin. Under 0.1 stable, over 0.25 significant, by convention
Projection A derived copy (search index, cache, graph) rebuilt from the source of truth, never edited
Provenance The full origin of a fact: source, file, page, model, time and rights
Puffin Iceberg's file format for statistics and deletion vectors
Quality card A summary of a dataset's health: freshness, completeness, corroboration, exceptions, straight-through rate
Quarantine A holding area for rows or files that failed checks, kept with reasons
RAG Retrieval-augmented generation: answering with retrieved passages as context
Ragas Library of RAG evaluation metrics: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, context recall
Rating outlook, watch A rating agency's view of a rating's likely direction (outlook), or a short-term review flag (watch)
Rating transition Movement of ratings between grades over time, studied as a matrix
RBI Reserve Bank of India: the central bank and banking regulator
Recall, precision Share of true items found / share of returned items that are right
Recovery Amount recovered after a default, often as a percentage
Redaction Removing or masking sensitive values before data leaves the perimeter
Redistribute (right) Licence permission to pass data on to third parties
Reranker A model that re-orders top search results by relevance
Restatement A source officially revising previously published figures, such as restated financials
REST catalog The Iceberg REST protocol for catalogs (03)
Revision analytics Studying how figures changed between versions, and who restates or drifts
Row filter A function that hides rows depending on who is asking
Row lineage Iceberg v3 per-row ids and last-updated sequence numbers
RRF Reciprocal rank fusion: combining rankings by summing 1/(k + rank)
SCD Slowly changing dimension. Type 1 overwrites, Type 2 keeps versioned history
Scheme, plan, option A mutual fund product / its direct or regular plan / its growth or IDCW option
SEBI Securities and Exchange Board of India: the securities regulator
Securitisation pool, tranche A bundle of loans sold to investors / a slice of it with its own risk and priority
Semantic layer Shared definitions of metrics and dimensions over the data
Sequence number (Iceberg) Number ordering commits, used to apply deletes correctly
Shredding Storing common fields of a variant value as typed columns (04)
Signed vintage A dataset release whose manifest is cryptographically signed, so it can be verified later
Skill (agent) Published instructions telling an agent when and how to use tools
SLM Small language model, roughly 3 to 14 billion parameters, often self-hosted
Snapshot The state of an Iceberg table after one commit
Split Dividing each share into several. Prices adjust, so history must be adjusted
Store (right) Licence permission to keep a copy of the data
Straight-through rate Share of data that passed every gate without a person touching it
Streaming table A Lakeflow table that processes each new input once
Style drift A fund's holdings moving away from its declared style or category
Survivorship Rules deciding which source's value wins for each attribute of a golden record
Synced table A table kept in sync between Unity Catalog and Lakebase Postgres
System tables Unity Catalog tables of audit, lineage, billing and job history

5. T to Z

Term Meaning
Table format A specification turning a folder of files into a reliable table: Iceberg, Delta, Hudi
Tag (Iceberg) A named, fixed snapshot, for example a certified release
Taxonomy A hierarchy of categories, without the rich relationships of an ontology
Text-to-SQL Generating SQL from a natural-language question, then validating and running it read-only
Tool poisoning Malicious instructions hidden in an agent tool's description or schema
Time travel Reading a table as of an earlier snapshot or time
Tool type, tool instance Agent capability built once in code / a configured, approved use of it
TRI Total return index: an index including reinvested dividends or coupons
Triangulation Comparing a fact across sources and scoring agreement
UniForm Delta tables that also write Iceberg metadata for Iceberg readers
Unity Catalog Databricks' governance layer for data and AI objects (05)
Update (versus correction) A normal new value, such as tomorrow's NAV, not a fix
UPI Unified Payments Interface. Aggregate volumes are published monthly
Valid time When a fact was true in the world
Variant Semi-structured data type in Parquet, Iceberg v3, Delta and Spark 4
Vector search Finding passages whose embeddings are near the question's embedding
Versioning (storage) Keeping prior versions of each object when it is overwritten or deleted
Vintage A frozen, named release of a dataset that clients receive
VLM Vision-language model: reads images and text together, for hard pages
Volume A Unity Catalog object for governed non-tabular files
WAP Write-audit-publish: write somewhere hidden, check, then publish atomically
Watermark The point up to which a stream or incremental load has processed data
WORM Write once, read many: storage that can't be modified or deleted during retention
Yield curve Yields of bonds of one issuer type across maturities
Zero-copy Sharing data between engines or tables without duplicating bytes

6. Easily confused pairs

Pair Difference
Update / correction / restatement Normal new value / fix of our error or the source's error / official revision by the source
Valid time / knowledge time When it was true / when we knew it
Snapshot / vintage Technical state after any commit (expires) / business release that is certified and kept
Taxonomy / ontology Category tree / full model of concepts and relationships
Managed / external / foreign table UC owns the files / UC governs your files / another catalog owns the metadata
Copy-on-write / merge-on-read Rewrite on change / mark deletes, merge on read
Row filter / column mask Hides rows / hides or alters values
Precision / recall Of what we returned, how much is right / of what is true, how much we found

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. What is the difference between a snapshot and a vintage?
  2. Which right must a source grant before its data goes out through a share?
  3. What does a deletion vector replace?
  4. Define straight-through rate.
  5. What does survivorship decide?

Answers

  1. A snapshot is any commit's technical state, and expires. A vintage is a named, certified release that is kept.
  2. Redistribute.
  3. Multiple v2 position-delete files per data file.
  4. The share of data that passed every gate without a person touching it.
  5. Which source's value wins for each attribute of a golden record.

8. Sources

The definitions are original summaries. Product and standard terms follow the official sources cited in chapters 01 to 13 (checked 2026-10-26). Regulatory terms follow the RBI, SEBI and AMFI public websites.
